notes:
Summary: Glacier Realtime Solutions — POC for low-latency customer-support + trading-desk assistant. Primary constraint: strict p95 latency target for streaming responses (requirement: p95 <= 200ms end-to-end; token flush <= 60ms). Workload: concurrent live sessions, avg session length 400 tokens, burst to 200 req/s.

Timeline and recent activities:
- 2025-11-04: Initial inbound via website trial; AE outreach (Maya C.).
- 2025-11-18: Discovery call — product/infra. Confirmed VPC requirement + KMS. SE Liam joined.
- 2025-12-01: Technical deep-dive; received sample traffic traces (gRPC streaming).
- 2025-12-10: POC kickoff (Fireflies ff_2025-12-10_glacier-eval-call). Trial config: dedicated pool w/ batching tuned for 1-2 token latency window.
- 2025-12-15 to 2026-01-22: POC runs; Redwood snapshot + profiling attached to drive. Multiple tuning passes (kernel selection, batching, prefix caching).
- 2026-01-25: SE report: observed generation p95 700-1200ms across workloads; streaming chunk emission irregular (0.6-1.2s gaps), intermittent 5-10s stalls on long context windows.
- 2026-02-04: Glacer infra team escalated to security review — requested SOC2 type II evidence and network flow diagrams. Delivered docs but internal procurement slowed.
- 2026-02-10: Competitor demo (RivalAI) — they showcased edge routing + pre-warmed model routing; Glacier cited lower p95 in their test.
- 2026-02-14: Final decision communicated: Glacier selects RivalAI (faster time-to-prod and committed latency SLA); budget freeze & org reorg removed champion.

Technical notes / root causes identified:
- Primary gap: end-to-end p95 not meeting target. Profiling indicates root cause spread across: kernel selection for long context, batching heuristics increasing tail latency under burst, and streaming buffer/flush behavior causing irregular chunk emission.
- Streaming: tokenization + flush policy mismatch led to large final-chunk delays for mid-session context switches. Connection keep-alive and gRPC flow-control interactions exacerbated tail latency.
- Attempts made: lowered batch windows, aggressive prefix cache, forced-quant path, and reduced context length in POC prompts — improved median but p95 still ~700ms.
- Infrastructure notes: Dedicated trial used NVidia A10x equivalent; Redwood team proposed private deployment with tighter kernel compilation but Glacier needed production SLA now.

Commercial/operational notes:
- Budget: stated ARR target for LLM infra $400k/year; procurement instituted Q1 freeze after cost re-prioritization.
- Champion: initially product lead (Sara H.) pushed for Redwood; reorganized in Jan and champion left. No internal successor.
- Decision drivers: latency SLA, speed to production, support for VPC + compliance. RivalAI offered edge routing + committed SLA in writing.

Next steps / recommended playbook:
- Mark as closed-lost; attach full POC profiling and short post-mortem to drive.
- Nurture: schedule 6-month touchpoint (Aug 2026) to share new bench reports (kernel improvements + streaming fixes).
- Win-back signals: thawed budget, new champion, requirement relaxation on residency.

Quote snippets from calls:
- "We need p95 under 200ms or we can't route live trades — latency isn't negotiable." — Glacier infra lead
- "Your streaming chunks were good in median but the stalls caused our demo to look flaky." — Product manager

Open tasks for Redwood (internal):
- Attach INF-1238/INF-1249 ticket logs and final POC perf dumps to the account folder.
- Prepare short-run bench that demonstrates p95 improvements for long-context streaming (due 2026-08).

Status: Closed-lost (technical SLO not met + competitor picked + budget freeze + no champion). Follow-up: nurture, reengage if procurement reopens or new champion surfaces.
